assessments.reasoning: The edition-specific original at https://www.latex-project.org/lppl/lppl-1-3a.txt identifies “LPPL Version 1.3a  2004-10-01” and “Copyright 1999 2002-04 LaTeX3 Project.” Capture 571e5cb16d73405aa49b41ae8e6bb20d at 2026-11-28T11:15:02Z returned HTTP 200 and one UTF-8 body from the title through the final “   the Work.\n\n”. Its single range [0,18435) and whole-file receipt both report SHA-256 06403f8c2fd53f994c4a424a8eaa65175062afc96422671f60374f4baf16091a. The publisher and copyright identify the authority, the header supplies the legal rule, and the digest selects the exact artifact. The identical grant in 1.3c alone cannot identify 1.3a.

challenge.method: Checked the edition-specific publisher URL, header, copyright and end of file. Examined the preamble’s “small modifications” wording, the permission to use the text as a model, the Current Maintainer’s powers and the example notice for exceptions to the header. Compared the example and digest with 1.3c to detect edition substitution.
challenge.results: The preamble discusses applying the license to a holder’s work. The model-text paragraph expressly describes drafting a different license. Maintainer powers concern the defined Work. The 1.3a example uses “Copyright 2003 M. Y. Name,” offers version 1.3 or later, and mentions LaTeX 2003/12/01 or later. Its three pig files and maintainer illustrate a hypothetical project. None of these passages excludes material from the verbatim-copy grant or authorizes publishing an edited document as LPPL 1.3a.

limitations: The finding covers the specified publisher file. Applying LPPL to an actual work requires the appropriate holder’s decisions about the notice, version, maintainer and files.

All five originals were delivered directly as full UTF-8 text in five separate captures, each including its header and final line. The three policy captures reported single full ranges of 14,088, 6,440 and 1,219 bytes at commit ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710. Source lengths and SHA-256 values were checked against acquisition receipts. The prescribed five-call procedure did not include a separate local hash calculation or an audit of the earlier research execution.
reasoning: LPPL 1.3a expressly permits everyone to distribute verbatim copies of “this license document” and prohibits modification of it. A byte-for-byte copy of the identified file satisfies that wording and preserves the copyright notice, examples and final recommendations. The controlling passage is the two-line grant immediately below the LaTeX3 Project copyright, at lines 7–8.
